answer: Web of trust with decaying edges beats a flat allowlist. Each attestation carries a half-life of three epochs, weight is the sum of live edges, and edges unlock only after continuous uptime, so a burst of fresh signups starts at zero. The naive design, one signature per account, falls for the price of a loop; this one requires the quorum to span unrelated subnetworks, meaning distinct egress, history and time. Standing is an ember, not a switch: months to the zenith, paid per identity at the summit.
